title: IFFI opens in Goa on Friday with Pawlikowski's 'Fatherland'; Dhurandhar leads Indian Panorama
dek: The 57th International Film Festival of India runs from 20 to 28 November with 159 international films from 86 countries, 76 Indian films in 18 languages and a new focus on BRICS cinema.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) opens in Goa on Friday, 20 November, with Fatherland, a black-and-white drama by the Polish director Paweł Pawlikowski that won him a share of the Best Director award at Cannes this year. The festival runs until 28 November under the theme "Stories Without Borders" and will show 159 films from 86 countries, chosen from about 1,400 submissions, the festival director, Ashutosh Gowariker, said at the curtain-raiser, according to the Press Information Bureau (PIB).

Alongside the international programme, 76 Indian films in 18 languages will be screened in the Indian Cinema sections, the PIB said. The Indian Panorama opens with Dhurandhar, the Hindi feature directed by Aditya Dhar, and, in the non-feature category, Becoming. The festival is organised by the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC) under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.

## The opening and closing films

Fatherland is set in the summer of 1949. It follows the Nobel Prize-winning German writer Thomas Mann and his daughter Erika, an actress, writer and rally driver, on a road trip through a divided Germany after his 16 years of exile in the United States, from US-run Frankfurt to Soviet-controlled Weimar. The 82-minute film, a co-production of Poland, Germany, Italy and France, stars Sandra Hüller and Hanns Zischler and will have its India premiere at the festival, the PIB said. It has also been shown at San Sebastián and Telluride.

The mid-festival film is I Matter, by the Romanian director Alina Șerban, a Romania-Germany-Belgium co-production in Romanian and Romani. The festival closes with We Are All Strangers by the Singaporean director Anthony Chen, according to reports.

## What else is on

- Films from BRICS: a new 21-film showcase from the bloc's member and partner countries, opened by Ramayana: Part One. It includes films from Brazil, Indonesia, South Africa, Iran, Saudi Arabia, China, Russia, Egypt, Vietnam and the UAE, among others.
- Country of Honour, Spain: four films, including Pedro Almodóvar's Bitter Christmas.
- Partner Country, Russia: a four-film showcase.
- Two new sections, Animation and Films About Films, with five films each.
- A five-film retrospective for the birth centenary of the Polish director Andrzej Wajda, including Ashes and Diamonds, Man of Marble and Kanal, according to reports.

The festival received more than 1,900 submissions from 137 countries across its sections, the PIB said. The Indian Panorama selection drew 404 feature and 358 non-feature entries, and 46 eligible entries were received for the Best Web Series (OTT) award.

## Competitions and prizes

The International Competition jury is chaired by the Hindi film director Aanand L. Rai. The winning film takes the Golden Peacock and Rs 51 lakh; the best director receives a Silver Peacock and Rs 20 lakh, according to reports. The Best Debut Feature competition has seven entries, two of them Indian: The Sledge and Birds on Ice. The festival also awards the ICFT-UNESCO Gandhi Medal.

For the Indian Panorama, the feature film jury is chaired by Madhur Bhandarkar and the non-feature jury by Himanshu Shekhar Khatua, the PIB said.

Ramayana: Part One, which opens the BRICS section, has been in cinemas since Diwali and earned more in its second weekend than its first, according to trade estimates.

Goa Chief Minister Pramod Sawant said at the curtain-raiser that the state had arranged screening venues, transport, hospitality and public facilities for visitors, according to the PIB.
